newsitem.title: USA: Roberts Oil buys Colombian stake.
newsitem.headline: Roberts Oil buys Colombian stake.

text.p: Roberts Oil and Gas Inc said Tuesday it purchased 100 percent of the Chimichagua Association Contract in Colombia from Geopozos SA for an undisclosed amount of stock.

The contract covers 211,000 acres in the lower Magdalena Valley, the company said, adding the eight wells drilled there have resulted in two natural gas discoveries with proven reserves put at 33.2 billion cubic feet of gas and probable reserves at 303 billion cubic feet.
The two discovery wells tested 9.0 and 3.4 million cubic feet of gas per day, respectively, Roberts said.
This acquisition "places us in a very strong position to acquire additional concession contracts in what we consider to be an undeveloped oil and gas-rich region," said President Earl Roberts.
"This also positions Roberts to participate in power generation projects in what is now a power-deficient area and enables us to be an integral part of the industrialization efforts in Colombia."

Roberts Oil was incorporated in 1980 for the purpose of engaging in the exploration, development and production of oil and natural gas. During the prolonged industry recession, Roberts said, it concentrated on reducing debt while participating as a working interest or royalty owner in 140 active wells located primarily in Texas and Oklahoma.
The company said it has 20 million shares authorized and 10 million have been issued, including those used to acquire the Colombian contract. ((-- New York Newsdesk 212-859-1610.))
